issues.legal_issue: A person recorded in occupation during the relevant revenue-record period may acquire statutory adhivasi rights when continued possession under appellate stay orders remains in the person's asserted right rather than on behalf of the court, and an entry describing the person as a thekadar does not by itself establish possession on behalf of the lessor.
material_facts: The claimant had been in possession under a theka, which had expired before the relevant revenue-record period.

After an ejectment decree, the claimant remained in possession because appellate courts stayed execution of the decree; the claimant had been in possession before the decree and continued to assert its own tenancy right.
The claimant was recorded in the revenue records as being in possession as a thekadar and was also in actual possession during the relevant period.
The claimant sought possession on the basis of statutory adhivasi rights.
issues.conclusion: The claimant acquired adhivasi rights and was entitled to possession. Its possession continued under the stay orders in the same right it had asserted before the ejectment decree, not on behalf of the court. The thekadar entry did not prevent the court from considering other evidence about the nature of its possession; on the facts, the claimant occupied in its own right and not on behalf of the landlords. The court therefore did not need to decide whether the claimant also qualified under the separate hereditary-tenancy provision, and the related ejectment appeal was dismissed as infructuous.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 20(b)(i) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, a person recorded as an occupant in the specified revenue records may become an adhivasi and, subject to the Act, take or retain possession; section 232 provides a procedure for an eligible adhivasi to seek possession. “Occupant” bears its ordinary meaning, subject to the limitation that the person must occupy in their own right and not on behalf of another. A stay that allows a person already in possession to remain there does not, without more, make that possession possession on behalf of the court. The nature of possession is not determined conclusively by an entry describing the person as a thekadar, and other evidence may be considered. The court relied on Swami Prasad v. Board of Revenue, U.P.; distinguished Parshotam Das v. Prem Narain, where a receiver had been appointed; and discussed Birjlal v. Murli Pd. and Lala Nanak Chand v. The Board of Revenue, U.P., without deciding the correctness of the latter decision on whether actual possession was required.

rule.if: claim_for_statutory_adhivasi_status and recorded_in_relevant_land_records and actual_possession_during_record_period and possession_began_before_ejectment_order and appellate_stay_preserved_possession and claimant_asserted_own_tenancy and lease_ended_before_record_period

predicates.claim_for_statutory_adhivasi_status: The person sought statutory recognition as an adhivasi and the resulting right to possession.
predicates.recorded_in_relevant_land_records: The person was recorded in the relevant land records as occupying the land.
predicates.actual_possession_during_record_period: The person was in actual possession of the land during the period covered by the relevant records.
predicates.possession_began_before_ejectment_order: The person was already in possession before an order for ejectment was made.
predicates.appellate_stay_preserved_possession: An appellate court's stay orders enabled the person to remain in possession after the ejectment order.
predicates.claimant_asserted_own_tenancy: The person resisted ejectment by asserting a tenancy right of their own.
predicates.lease_ended_before_record_period: The lease or tenancy arrangement under which the person had originally entered had ended before the relevant record period.

issues.definition: When a person seeking statutory adhivasi status is recorded and actually present in possession, had entered possession before an ejectment order, remained there under appellate stays while asserting a tenancy right of their own, and the underlying lease had ended before the relevant record period, the person acquires adhivasi status.
